texts: Somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP) travel up the dorsal columns, so they detect ischaemia only in the back of the spinal cord: A.
Paraplegia comes from ischaemia of the anterior cord, fed by the anterior spinal artery and the artery of Adamkiewicz, the kiwi; the sheep on the back lane notices nothing.
Motor evoked potentials (MEP), the motorbike on the front lane, test that motor path and are more accurate than SSEP.
Draining cerebrospinal fluid lowers the rate of paraplegia, and distal aortic perfusion improves on clamp-and-sew in extensive repairs.
Profound hypothermia with circulatory arrest has not proved clearly better than moderate hypothermia with partial bypass.
Memory hook: the sheep strolls along the back of the cable; only the motorbike notices when the front goes dark.
